explanation: Fires on a word-initial 'K'/' k' token that starts a word split into subword pieces, often a foreign or loan word or a proper noun (Kiso, kring, kudos, KGB, Kobe, Konto, Kaffee, Künstler). It fires weaker on other first fragments of split words (vel-cro, Bel-voir, Ohl) and on some CJK characters. Ordinary whole-word tokens do not activate it.

No clear shared feature. It fires on Russian grammatical endings and function words inside programming Q&A text (больш-ей, мо-ем, было, код), on digits and odd tokens in code or identifiers (rfc1034, 0x1c, Ruby200, ' :scope', assembly whitespace), and on fragments of medical words and names (phyto-hem, Hem-ophilia, plasm-acy, Me-ad, J-um-ana).

Fires on a noun or content word that completes a noun phrase or object, especially plural nouns naming components or contents (columns, fields, answers, microtransactions, sugar, veins, enzymes, cells, pixels, space), and on some code tokens in argument lists. Activation is moderate and spread out. Function words in the middle of a phrase give weak or no activation.

Fires on the token that opens a contrast or limitation clause after background has been set up, typically in abstracts ('Despite', 'Although', 'However,', 'limited', 'but it is relatively weak') and in problem reports ('not firing', 'can only', 'it's not working', 'doesn't run'). It fires most strongly on 'Despite'/'Although' at the start of a sentence in a scientific abstract.

Fires on tokens that continue or close an open-ended list or enumeration: 'among other', 'and so on', 'plus', 'or its affiliates', 'the other', 'something like it', '\ldots'. Separately, it fires on separator or continuation tokens in formatted strings: digits inside version or hash numbers (SHA-256, 4.0.30319.1), time-format separators (':mm', ':'), and '+' at the start of ASCII table borders.

Fires on the middle or final subword piece of a rare or technical word, or a fixed-phrase completion, where the rest of the word is fully predictable from what came before (Lat-v-ian, ghre-lin, therm-oplast-ics, nor-ve-gicus, gall-bl-adder, scrot-al, Beh-old, State Highway, writ of mandamus, Fed. R. App.). The common thread is predictable continuation, not one particular token.

Fires mainly on the token that closes a source-code header comment block (' */', '*/', '//' after license or copyright text), right before code starts. The top example is 'Edition' in 'Kindle Edition', and it fires weakly on scattered other tokens.

Fires on byte-fragment tokens of non-Latin multibyte characters (CJK, Devanagari, Greek symbols shown as broken bytes), and on the first subword piece after a hyphen or of a split word in European text and biomedical terms (France-P-resse, cross-p-resentation, an-ap-lastic, d-ip-henyl, r-hamnosus, Fl-üchtlinge). In both cases the unit is a word-internal fragment that begins a multi-token word.

Fires on the second or later piece of a technical compound or word (pesticide residue, octah-edral, transesophage-al, Huffman, bibli-ography, Chi-squared, head-up) and on specific code tokens (' =' in a static field initializer, '.close', ')arg', 'templates'). Other strong examples include the date comma in 'Joined: Wed Apr 21,' and 'fleeing', 'World War', 'tall'. There is no single shared concept.

Fires on coordinators and number words inside enumerations of a counted set: ' and', ' &' or ',' joining listed names or items ('Jono and Sushu', 'LmrC and LmrD', '66.7%, and'), and count words like 'three', 'two', '2 w' when an earlier number sets up a group. It is strongest when a count precedes a list of members.

A diffuse mixture. It fires on ' =' in PHP and Obj-C assignments, on '.' in legal citation abbreviations (L. REV., F.2d, No.), on plural endings in citation keys (microm-achines, polym-ers), and on various tokens in boilerplate web or legal text (Dashboard., Enjoy, located, Rendered on). There is no single unifying context.

Fires on function words (a, the, and, on, by, of, ',') that come right after or near a mention of a color, especially 'white' and 'black' ('black text on a white', 'black and white', 'White film on', 'white nationalist'). The unit seems to track the context of a recent white/black color word rather than the token itself, and it fires weakly in other color contexts.

Fires on tokens in descriptive or clinical prose, often a function word or modifier just before a noun phrase about a physical or medical process ('slowly drains', 'such as acute', 'nose and the paranasal', 'rain began to fall', 'obstruction of the upper airway'). It also fires on assorted narrative tokens. The pattern is unclear.

Fires on a word-internal subword piece in the middle of a rare proper name or technical term, usually a foreign surname, place name or biochemical word (Svarth-ol-m, Car-lu-cci, Mol-ot, H-il-bert, sc-opol-amine, immun-osorbent, prolifer-ator, d-ou-geby). It fires weaker on scattered function words.
